introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in the question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 23/0595/3/Grp 1 to Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing), Task II (spreadsheet) and Task III (a short exercise on HTML, on a database or on a C or Pascal program). The working files named in the tasks (the picture UN.jpg, the pictures of the authors) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP THREE - TASK I (20 marks)**

Text to type (a title, an opening paragraph, a four-item list, two sub-headings with their paragraphs and the author line):

> Modern Developments in the use of Internet
>
> The Internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks that use the standard Internet protocol suite (TCP/IP) to serve billions of users worldwide. It is a network of networks that consists of millions of private, public, academic, business, and government networks, of local to global scope, that are linked by a broad array of electronic, wireless and optical networking technologies. The Internet carries an extensive range of information resources and services, such as the inter-linked hypertext documents of the World Wide Web (WWW) and the infrastructure to support email.
>
> Some important modern developments in the use of Internet are given below:
>
> - Web Browsers
> - ISPs
> - Social Networking
> - Digital Media Sharing Websites
>
> ***Web Browsers*** (bold, italic and underlined sub-heading)
>
> A web browser can be defined as an application software or program designed to enable users to access, retrieve and view documents and other resources on the Internet. An information resource is identified by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) and may be a web page, image, video, or other piece of content. Hyperlinks present in resources enable users easily to navigate their browsers to related resources. The major web browsers are Firefox, Google Chrome, Internet Explorer, Opera, and Safari
>
> ***Internet Service Providers (ISPs)*** (bold, italic and underlined sub-heading)
>
> An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is an organization that provides access to the Internet. Internet service providers can be either community-owned and non-profit, or privately owned and for-profit. Access ISPs directly connect clients to the Internet using copper wires, wireless or fiber optic connections. Transit ISPs provide large amounts of bandwidth for connecting hosting ISPs to access ISPs.
>
> By Susan Hook
incertitudes: Structure du lot : les quatre PDF fournis sont nommes DAY1 a DAY4, mais les pages de garde imprimees parlent de GROUPES (« Group Two », « Group Three », « Group Four », livrets 23/0595/3/Grp 2, 3 et 4), pas de jours. Un seul dossier, douze fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1 a G4-T3 (groupe n, tache m), groupes ["GROUP 1"] a ["GROUP 4"] (et non D<n>-T<m> / ["DAY n"]). regles_choix est vide : le candidat ne passe qu'un seul groupe, ce qui n'est pas exprimable.

Le PDF DAY1 (Group One) n'a que 3 pages et pas de page de garde (il commence a la page 2 du livret, « Do all the tasks... ») : le niveau et la matiere sont verifies par la reference imprimee en pied de page (0000/0595/3/Grp 1, soit le code 0595) et par la structure identique aux trois autres groupes. La duree de 2 h 30 est reprise des pages de garde des groupes 2, 3 et 4 (« Two and a Half hours »).

Aucun corrige officiel n'existe : les reponses sont redigees. Les « marking ideas » sont des repartitions indicatives faites d'apres les points imprimes ; le bareme du jury n'est pas connu. Les fichiers de donnees du jour (image UN.jpg, photos des auteurs, dossier du candidat) ne sont pas dans le PDF ; aucun logiciel (traitement de texte, tableur, gestionnaire de base de donnees, navigateur, compilateur) n'a ete execute : les menus sont donnes sous leur forme generale (Office / LibreOffice recents), de memoire, sans version de logiciel affirmee.

Les filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo), les cadres d'en-tete (numero de centre, nom du candidat, « For examiners' use only »), les lignes a completer et les artefacts du scanner (scans sans couche texte, photos de feuilles legerement inclinees) sont ignores. Chaque PDF a ete lu page par page en image.

Tous les resultats chiffres (colonnes calculees, classements, comptages, totaux) ont ete recalcules avec Python a partir des donnees imprimees, en fractions exactes pour les moyennes ; les formules de tableur ont ete traduites en Python (SUM, AVERAGE, RANK, IF, COUNTIF). Les points imprimes de chaque tache somment bien au total annonce (voir ci-dessous) ; aucun point imprime n'a ete corrige.

Group Three, Task I : points imprimes 7, 2, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2 = 20, comme annonce. Le texte est celui de Susan Hook (titre « Modern Developments in the use of Internet », sans « the », avec deux sous-titres : Web Browsers et Internet Service Providers (ISPs)). Dans le sujet, « Opera, and Safari » n'est pas suivi d'un point : repris tel quel. Les sous-titres sont imprimes en gras, italique et souligne (decrit dans l'enonce). Le sujet dit « Save as Task I » en (b) puis « Task 1b » en (d) : repris tel quel. « Drop caps at the start of each paragraph » est lu comme les trois paragraphes du corps du texte (pas la ligne d'introduction de la liste) : lecture a confirmer par le bareme du jury, inconnu. La photo de l'auteure n'est pas fournie.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch the word processor on your computer and type the text above. Save as Task I. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open the word processor and a new blank document.

1. Type the title, the opening paragraph, the line "Some important modern developments in the use of Internet are given below:", the four list lines, the two sub-headings (**Web Browsers** and **Internet Service Providers (ISPs)**), their two paragraphs and the author line "By Susan Hook", exactly as printed. Press *Enter* only at the end of a paragraph.
2. Check the spelling and compare with the printed text.
3. *File* > *Save As* > file name **Task I** > *Save*.

Marking idea (7 marks): the three long paragraphs typed (3); title, list lines, sub-headings and author line (2); accuracy (1); file saved as Task I (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the document as follows: set page size to A4, and page orientation to Landscape. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Layout* > **Size** > **A4**, then *Layout* > **Orientation** > **Landscape**. In *LibreOffice Writer*: *Format* > *Page Style* > *Page*: format A4, orientation Landscape.

Marking idea (2 marks): A4 (1); Landscape (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Set top and left margins to 1.5 cm each. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Layout* > **Margins** > *Custom Margins*: **Top = 1.5 cm**, **Left = 1.5 cm** > *OK*.

Marking idea (1 mark): both margins 1.5 cm.

questions.enonce_markdown: The title should be bold and centred, and formatted with a 14-point serif font and inserted as a header. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. *Insert* > **Header** > *Blank* (or *Edit Header*): the header is the area at the top of every page, outside the body of the text.
2. In the header, type the title **Modern Developments in the use of Internet** (or cut it from the text and paste it there, so that it appears only once).
3. Select it and format: **B** (Bold), **Center** (*Ctrl + E*), a **serif** font (for example *Times New Roman*) and size **14**. Close the header.

Marking idea (3 marks): title placed in the header (1); bold and centred (1); 14-point serif font (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: The paragraphs should be left- and right-justified, have a line spacing of 1.5, and be formatted with a 12-point serif font. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the paragraphs of the body text and:

1. **Justify** (*Ctrl + J*): aligned on both the left and right margins.
2. *Paragraph* > **Line spacing 1.5**.
3. Font **Times New Roman** (serif), size **12**.

Marking idea (3 marks): justified (1); line spacing 1.5 (1); 12-point serif font (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert picture of author and the name, centralized at the top of the page. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The picture of the author is supplied on the day; it is not reproduced here.

1. Put the cursor at the beginning of the body text (the first line of the page) and press *Enter* to make room.
2. *Insert* > **Pictures** > select the author's picture > *Insert*; resize it in proportion (drag a corner with *Shift* held).
3. Select the picture and click **Center** (*Ctrl + E*), then type the name **Susan Hook** on the line below the picture and centre it too.

Marking idea (2 marks): picture and name inserted at the top of the page (1); both centred (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a drop cap (2 lines) at the start of each paragraph. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A drop cap is a large first letter that sinks into the paragraph over several lines. For each paragraph of the body text (the opening paragraph, the Web Browsers paragraph and the Internet Service Providers paragraph):

1. Click inside the paragraph.
2. *Insert* > **Drop Cap** > *Dropped* > *Drop Cap Options*: **Lines to drop = 2** > *OK* (in *LibreOffice Writer*: *Format* > *Paragraph* > *Drop Caps*, 2 lines).
3. Repeat for the other paragraphs.

Marking idea (2 marks): drop cap of 2 lines on the first paragraph (1); on each of the other paragraphs (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your document as Task 1b. *[no mark printed]*

questions.corrige_markdown: *File* > *Print*: check the preview (landscape page, header, picture and name at the top, drop caps), then click *Print*.
